title: Scale-wise Distillation of Diffusion Models
claim: Noise masks high-frequency content of signals, so high-noise timesteps can be processed at reduced resolution without losing information.
layout: 4 side-by-side log-log power spectrum plots (2 SD3.5 spatial, 2 Wan2.1 spatial/temporal), shared legend, shaded red/green frequency regions with dotted boundary lines
description: Four log-log line plots show power versus frequency. The first two panels are SD3.5 latents at timesteps t=600 and t=800, plotted against spatial frequency. The third panel is Wan2.1 at t=600 against spatial frequency. The fourth panel is Wan2.1 at t=600 against temporal frequency. Each panel has three curves: noise (flat blue), noisy latents (orange) and clean latents (purple). The purple curve falls steeply, and the orange curve meets the flat noise floor at higher frequencies. Dotted red and green vertical lines mark frequency boundaries. The region between them is shaded pink, and the region to the right of the green line is shaded green. Labels give the resolution and reduction factor, such as 32×32 4×↓ and 80×80 1.6×↓. The eye goes first to the colored bands and the crossing of the curves.
caption: Spectral analysis of SD3.5 VAE latents ($128{\times}128$) (Left) and Wan2.1 ($21{\times}60{\times}104$) for spatial and temporal dimensions (Right). Vertical lines mark the frequency boundaries for which the frequency components to the right are not present in lower resolution latents. Noise masks high frequencies, suggesting that latent DMs can operate at lower latent resolutions for high noise levels. Green area indicates the allowed latent resolution at corresponding timestep, while Red area shows that further resolution reduction would lead to noticeable information loss.
abstract: Recent diffusion distillation methods have achieved remarkable progress, enabling high-quality ${\sim}4$-step sampling for large-scale text-conditional image and video diffusion models. However, further reducing the number of sampling steps becomes more and more challenging, suggesting that efficiency gains may be better mined along other model axes. Motivated by this perspective, we introduce SwD, a scale-wise diffusion distillation framework that equips few-step models with progressive generation, avoiding redundant computations at intermediate diffusion timesteps. Beyond efficiency, SwD enriches the family of distribution matching distillation approaches by introducing a simple patch-level distillation objective based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). This objective significantly improves the convergence of existing distillation methods and performs surprisingly well in isolation, offering a competitive baseline for diffusion distillation. Applied to state-of-the-art text-to-image/video diffusion models, SwD approaches the sampling speed of two full-resolution steps and largely outperforms alternatives under the same compute budget, as evidenced by automatic metrics and human preference studies. Project page: https://yandex-research.github.io/swd
